# Thunderbird history batch 003: behavior and syntax

Source: `Thunderbird comm checkout`, clean checkout on `Bug-2061213_2`; `origin/main` was `6ccc9d3f07d89f3d05984c119f20788417cecceb` on 2026-10-06. From the parent of batch 002's `fa682aa39bf108bb41c2b595461f9b66021c3583`, inspect 1,000 more first-parent, non-merge, human-authored commits: `f21d73b2965e761bea677a7fdba9520d4004dc5c` (2026-08-20) through `8999e70bcbb39b63a45eb42624b5a9c305552d11` (2026-04-20). Skip 271 automation/bulk vendor-sync commits. Next cursor: `8999e70bcbb39b63a45eb42624b5a9c305552d11^`. Of the 1,000, 921 link to 900 distinct Phabricator reviews; 79 lack a review link. A hidden browser read complete timelines, including older changes, for 887 reviews; 13 were access-restricted. The visible timelines contain 5,171 comments, 4,846 from non-bot accounts. Do not infer from restricted reviews. Read representative landed diffs and tests in depth; indexed all landed diffs for repeated patterns. The code scan excludes third-party vendored code. Its counts include 21 backouts, so use backouts as breakage evidence, not style examples.

## How the code works; breakage lessons

- A storage Calendar can still receive a read after `profile-change-teardown`. Reading `params` on a finalized SQLite statement can assert or crash. Guard the statement's state before parameter access; a stream may swallow only the known shutdown error, not arbitrary failures. The regression test deliberately avoids first use before teardown. [commit](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/commit/42a5262682fdc8c60bc5232dfd959eb8401af632), [D317485](https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D317485).
- Cached ICS must restore offline changes into the recreated cache before server playback, await additions while its observer batch is open, and let one rejected item leave other items available. ICS/CalDAV cached callbacks must be taken and cleared per operation so a later playback cannot reuse an old callback and delete the wrong event. For overwrite, `modifyItem(item, null)` means overwrite current stored state; using `item` as its own base version can be rejected. [commit](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/commit/e543c863fd4f), [D310564](https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D310564), [D310485](https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D310485).
- A Calendar alarm acknowledgement may be absent from CalDAV after a server strips `X-MOZ-LASTACK`. Preserve a local acknowledgement timestamp and choose the later local/server value. Remove only legacy bare ignored-alarm entries, and mark migration complete only when cleanup actually occurs; `calendar.alarms.showmissed` affects whether cleanup should run. This was refined through review and tested for online-then-offline dismissal. [commit](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/commit/ac6cc8c5074c), [D311586](https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D311586).
- An IMAP-to-local move must let the destination delete the source only after copy success. Passing `moveMessage=true` to the source service also let it delete before a failed local copy, losing mail. Another fix synchronizes IMAP flags before setting the new-message count and delays new-mail notice for unselected folders until local flags catch up with server state. Tests check cross-server failure and server/client message state. [move commit](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/commit/20298d0e6306), [biff commit](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/commit/0bc9cf3ace02).
- IMAP OAuth shutdown can hang if the main-thread connection starts before its shutdown wake-up is registered; register the callback first and notify the waiting monitor at shutdown. IMAP subscription URLs hold weak folder references, so the new code keeps the folder alive through a URL listener. [shutdown commit](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/commit/24bda0b4f37b), [subscription commit](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/commit/3611f8c9773f).
- CalDAV response chunks are raw bytes. Decode once after assembling the whole body with the server's declared charset; decoding each chunk as UTF-8 fails for UTF-16 and split characters. Cross-origin DAV redirects with an `Authorization` header abort instead of carrying credentials to another server. [charset commit](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/commit/f65f05177086), [redirect commit](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/commit/cf52c835e3d5).
- Graph Calendar evolved from a hand-written `calICalendar` shell to `cal.provider.BaseClass`, then from a transient memory calendar toward the newer persistent/offline-backed delta design in batch 002. Read the later implementation before copying a pattern from this older batch. [base-class commit](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/commit/c29c640f11b4), [display commit](https://github.com/thunderbird/thunderbird-desktop/commit/23dea1d24bf1).

## Syntax evidence and decisions

Current configuration has priority over older diffs, then batch 001/002 (newer) over this batch. Thunderbird's shared Prettier config uses 80 columns, two spaces, `arrowParens: "avoid"`, and ES5 trailing commas; Calendar overrides to 100 columns. `.editorconfig` requires UTF-8, LF, final newline, and no trailing whitespace. `comm/eslint.config.mjs` enforces braces, `prefer-const`, object shorthand, JSDoc validation, module import checks, and browser-test `SpecialPowers.pushPrefEnv`; Calendar tests use UTC date APIs. `comm/.stylelintrc.js` enforces logical CSS properties and double-colon pseudo-elements; `fox/.clang-format` is Google-based at 80 columns with left pointer alignment. Use `../mach commlint --fix <path>` for comm files; D302199/D302333 show manual Prettier runs or `--outgoing` can miss the required local result. [D302199](https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D302199), [D302333](https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D302333).

In this 1,000-commit sample, 498 commits touch tests; 201 add named `add_task(async function test...)`, 270 add `Assert` calls, 127 add explicit state/event waits, 84 add cleanup functions, and 237 add documentation blocks. These are per-commit presence counts, not mandates or line totals. Batch 001 (100 commits) and 002 (500 commits) show the same patterns in their existing memory notes. A focused 11-diff syntax check of those older batches found 32 added named tasks, 133 `Assert` lines, and 95 `/**` lines; it did not rescan their reviews.

Review-backed syntax: write JSDoc on public component interfaces, use accurate `@param`/`@returns` types, and update it when names or behavior change (D298632, D297345, D306242). Use complete sentences and periods in explanatory comments, and keep them within the local line width (D304012). Name variables for the state they represent rather than a broad or opposite state (D293024, D317699). Name tests and assertions for observable behavior; use an assertion message that says what should happen. Use complete Fluent IDs in literals or a nearby comment so dynamic IDs stay searchable (D306242, D304559). A changed Fluent value or attribute needs a new ID and usually migration; keep punctuation in translated strings rather than CSS (D299482, D304921, D312939). Prefer existing CSS tokens and font-relative sizing where UI text must scale, but do not claim a blanket `rem` mandate: the sample adds many `px` values too (D295950, D308989).

Proposed future syntax rules, **not yet project-enforced**: in new JavaScript, use `const`/`let` rather than `var`; prefer `===`/`!==` unless a deliberate nullish/coercion check has a reason; use optional chaining only when absence is valid, not to hide a broken invariant; name every new async test task; keep one failure condition per assertion when separate values aid diagnosis; use meaningful boolean names; use a JSDoc block for exported/public functions and a short `//` comment for a surprising local reason; write CSS in logical properties and reuse existing design tokens before literals; prefer CSS classes to inline presentation except where Gecko chrome behavior requires inline style. Apply only to new or edited lines; do not demand mechanical rewrites of untouched legacy files. Review D302333 illustrates a platform-specific inline-style exception. Do not infer a global C++ or Rust naming rule from these commits; their local conventions and formatters govern.

Use this note for code and review work. For exact review comments, inspect the current patch and final landed/updated code: a browser timeline can show a requested change later rejected, revised, or superseded. The older commits in this batch are evidence about failures and intent; current config and newer code decide style when they differ.
